text:
incident-bot: Paging: elevated GPU node reboots + AER/ ECC errors observed in us-central1-gpu-pool. Severity: P1. Oncall: @oncall-sam. Pagerduty link: <https://pd.example/INC123456|INC123456>

oncall-sam: I’m on it. seeing 500+ failed requests for the pool, some customers reporting timeouts. starting triage.

sre-alex: Any automated mitigations started? I see autoscaler bouncing some VMs. logs show kernel AER events.

ops-julia: Customer impact note: SLAs for batch customers X & Y degraded ~20m ago. CS alerted them. @customer-success-liz tagging for comms.

customer-success-liz: Acknowledged. drafting a message now: will include ETA once we have root cause or mitigation.

infra-ryan: I’m pulling node-level diagnostics. running nvidia-smi and dmesg on the most recent failed host (gpunode-uc1-17).

eng-runtime-maya: Runtime metric: token latencies spiked ~3x and then requests fell to 0 for affected nodes. We have fallbacks but they’re overwhelmed.

oncall-sam: Immediate mitigations: (1) cordon gpunode-uc1-17, (2) drain running workloads to failover pool, (3) scale up healthy pool by 10% to absorb. Doing step 1 now.

ops-julia: cordon/drain in progress: `kubectl cordon gpunode-uc1-17` then `kubectl drain gpunode-uc1-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

infra-ryan: dmesg snippet from gpunode-uc1-17:
```
[ 1203.456789] pci 0000:3b:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=00e4
[ 1203.456790] pcieport 0000:3b:00.0: AER: Multiple Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error
[ 1204.789012] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 79, pid: 4221, grp: 0 
[ 1205.123456] kernel: GPU ecc error detected, candidate for soft reset
```

eng-runtime-maya: Also seeing KV cache invalidations around the same timestamps. Could be PCIe errors causing device resets, dropping sessions.

sre-alex: Looking at GCP agent logs: there are host reboots triggered within a minute of AER flood. suspect noisy neighbor causing PCIe bus congestion or firmware bug.

oncall-sam: Have we opened a cloud support case? If it's hardware-level we need provider escalation.

infra-ryan: Opening case now. Attaching host serial, dmesg, `lspci -vvv` and `nvidia-bug-report.sh`. Case ref 987654321. gcp-support-bot, can you confirm case creation?

 gcp-support-bot: Support case created: CASE-987654321. Assigned to GCP Infra Eng team. Priority: Critical.

ops-julia: Quick mitigation idea: move latency-sensitive traffic to eu-west pool while we investigate. Can we do cross-region failover for affected customers?

eng-runtime-maya: We have geo-fallback for some routes. Enabling cross-region routing for customer Y only (manual rollout) now. Expect reduced latency for those requests in ~5-10m.

customer-success-liz: Noting which customers we shifted: customer-Y (prod) now routed to eu-west. Customer-X is blocked due to data residency; we need to fix hosts quickly.

oncall-sam: Hypotheses so far (ranked):
- H1: PCIe AER flood from a noisy neighbor (VM/tenant saturating bus) -> device resets -> node reboot
- H2: GPU driver / firmware regression triggered by specific model/quantization kernel -> ECC errors -> kernel panic
- H3: Underlying host HW degradation (ECC DIMM or PCIe root complex failure)

sre-alex: Evidence: repeated AER entries + Xid 79 (GPU page fault) + immediate host reboots. H1 and H3 both plausible. Need to confirm if reboots happen on multiple hosts or localized.

infra-ryan: We have reboots on 5 nodes across two racks in us-central1 cluster-2: gpunode-uc1-17, -23, -29, -31, -44. Time window: 2026-11-03T14:12:30Z -> 14:18:00Z (UTC).

oncall-sam: Collect logs for all affected nodes and centralize to the incident bucket: gs://redwood-incident-logs/INC123456/. Please upload `dmesg`, `journalctl -k`, `nvidia-smi -q`, `lspci -vvv`, and `kern.log` for each host.

infra-ryan: Uploaded initial artifacts: <https://storage.example/INC123456/gpunode-uc1-17/dmesg.txt|gpunode-uc1-17 dmesg>, <https://storage.example/INC123456/manifest.txt|manifest>

eng-runtime-maya: I’ll run a stress repro on a non-prod replica with the same model config to see if we can provoke similar AER/Xid output. Will run for 30m.

ops-julia: Note: autoscaler already prevented replacing nodes automatically due to drain failures; we might need manual reprovisioning.

sre-alex: Action items: (A) collect host logs (assigned infra-ryan), (B) run repro (assigned eng-runtime-maya), (C) escalate to provider (oncall-sam + gcp-support-bot), (D) customer comms (customer-success-liz). Marking in-thread statuses as they progress.

infra-ryan: Quick grep across syslog shows repeated `pci_bus_error` for device 0000:3b:00.0 with code=0000. I’ll check neighbors on the same root port.

eng-runtime-maya: Repro run: after 12m load, observed similar Xid 79 and a soft-reset. Captured GPU trace and kernel oops. Uploading: <https://storage.example/INC123456/repro-run-20261103/logs|repro logs>

sre-alex: Good repro. That increases probability H2 (driver/firmware) or H1 (specific workload pattern) vs pure HW degradation. Need vendor-level debug on Xid 79.

gcp-support-bot: GCP update: investigating host-level metrics and PCIe bus errors. Asked on-call host tech to check for known firmware bug for this instance family.

oncall-sam: For immediate mitigation we will: 1) Quarantine affected racks (prevent scheduling), 2) Provision additional capacity in other zones, 3) Hold rolling upgrades/driver changes for now.

ops-julia: Quarantine done. Provisioning extra nodes in us-central1-b and us-central1-c to preserve locality.

customer-success-liz: Sent interim update to impacted customers: "We’re actively investigating GPU host instability; we have mitigations in flight and are engaging cloud support. Next update in 30m or on material change"

infra-ryan: Note for RCA: collect host firmware versions, PCIe root complex logs, ECC counters from IPMI if available, and GPU driver/firmware versions. Also check noisy neighbor telemetry (network/IO metrics) on co-located VMs.

eng-runtime-maya: I'll add reproducible inputs and a small test harness to help vendor debug. Also capturing kernel oops + GPU coredump.

sre-alex: Planning follow-ups: timeline reconstruction, mapping affected customers to hosts, correlate request traces to host timestamps, and collect BIOS/IPMI logs.

oncall-sam: If no new findings in 45m, we'll prepare a short RCA draft and list next steps (firmware roll, node replacement, provider escalations).

gcp-support-bot: GCP support note: Found a recent firmware advisory for this instance family referencing AER floods under heavy PCIe traffic. Recommend firmware patching; testing required.

oncall-sam: Thanks. Adding firmware advisory to the timeline as probable cause candidate.

customer-success-liz: Customers acknowledged, asking for ETA on full resolution. I’ll push the firmware advisory and next-steps in the next comms.

sre-alex: Logging final immediate state: impacted nodes quarantined, repro confirms AER/Xid 79 under load, cloud case open (CASE-987654321), firmware advisory identified. Moving to post-incident RCA channel once incident closed.

incident-bot: Incident INC123456: status=mitigated, severity=P1 -> P2, duration so far ~47m. Please update incident playbook with firmware check steps and noisy-neighbor detection heuristics.

oncall-sam: Closing this thread for live mitigation. Will create follow-up RCA thread with consolidated logs and timeline in ~2 hours. Thanks all. :tada:
